paraphrase: Abhinavagupta explains the Goddess's question as the Supreme questioning itself: the Unsurpassed (anuttara) is consciousness in which question and answer, teacher and disciple, are one; the letter A is the Unsurpassed and the universe unfolds from A to HA as the 'aham' (I).
notes: Summary of the commentary on the first verse; not verse-checked in detail.

paraphrase: Quoting other texts: the Trika is higher than the Kula; 'From the Veda the Śaiva, then the Vāma, then the Dakṣa, then the Kula, then the Mata, and then the Trika, supreme above all.'
notes: This variant places Mata after Kula; Jayaratha's quotation on TĀ 13.301 places Mata before Kula. Locator spot-checked in Phase B against a local e-text mirror in sources_raw/ (GRETIL / Muktabodha / DCS); not fidelity-checked; still a skeleton entry.
